d3.reset.r.p.r2.text: a responsibility she may not be used to
d3.reset.r.p.r2.why: The standard: additional responsibility that mainstream users may not be accustomed to.
d3.reset.r.p.r3.why: The standard has no "forgot password" button.
d3.reset.r.p.r4.why: Its goal is an alternative to identity providers.
d3.reset.r.p.r5.why: The standard promises none. It calls key management a hard problem.
d3.reset.r.prompt: What the standard hands her. Tap a chip, then its slot.
d3.slip: The supplier sums up: signing in with a key tells the site nothing about her. Samia wonders.
d3.stamp.prompt: The supplier's line again: signing in with a key tells the site nothing about her. Stamp it:
d3.stamp.reveal: Half. The message carries no name or email. It carries her address, and a reused address links her across sites.
row: One button asks a company to vouch for her; the other asks her own key to sign a message.
sticker.back: What it is: a standard message her wallet signs, so a site knows the account is hers. What you hold: the key that signs. What you give up: "forgot password", and privacy if one address goes everywhere. The wrong idea: every signature is a harmless sign-in. A standard, not a product. Named as an example, not a recommendation. Checked 2026-11-23.
